A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLHF Game and affine-maximizer mechanism. Their main text, equations, and complete appendices are readable, and retained results can be matched across restructuring and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 contains mathematical results, proofs, and implementation proposals, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes in either the main text or appendices.

after.justification: Section 5 reports original LLaMA2-7B experiments on Helpful Assistants and Reddit Summary tasks. Figure 2 presents resulting valuations, payments, and utilities under different reporting strategies.

M1.justification: v3 specifies SW-Max objectives through f-divergences and adds selection from a fixed candidate-model set constructed using parameter merging and decoding methods (Sections 4.4 and 5.2). The affine-maximizer payment and both earlier payment-computation approximations are retained.

E1.justification: v2 uses no empirical datasets. v3 adds Helpful Assistants using Anthropic-HH, with harmlessness and humor preferences, and Reddit Summary using Summarize-from-Feedback, with faithfulness and summary-quality preferences.

E2.justification: Figure 2 and Section 5.3 introduce an empirical zero-payment comparison: raw valuation represents utility without payments and is contrasted with utility after affine-maximizer payments. Rewarded Soups and Multi-Objective Decoding construct candidate models rather than serve as competing mechanisms.

E3.justification: v3 introduces an experimental protocol with two groups, fixed reports from the other group, group-size scaling by alpha, preference mixing by beta, and rewards normalized to [0,1]. Figure 2 evaluates three group-size pairs for Helpful Assistants and (7,3) for Reddit Summary; v2 has no corresponding protocol.

E4.justification: v3 adds systematic sensitivity analyses of group-size misreporting, preference misreporting, and group balance. Figure 2 examines how these changes affect valuation, payment, and utility, providing empirical incentive analyses absent from v2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new experimental plots add no uncertainty-reporting procedure; the bounded-noise guarantees are theoretical results.

E6.justification: v3 adds eight panels of valuation, payment, and utility results across four task/group-size settings. Figure 2 reports increased valuations under stronger reports, with payments making truthful reporting utility-maximizing among the tested strategies, often alongside tied plateaus. v2 contains no empirical results.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 is replaced by substantially revised necessity results and normalization-specific proofs (Theorems 4.2, 4.3, and A.2). v3 generalizes payment-equivalence conditions, replaces the L2 continuity example with chi-squared divergence, and revises the noise model to average across all groups while retaining the 2wi epsilon incentive bound. Cycle monotonicity is retained in Appendix D.

C1.justification: The central no-payment claim shifts from strong dominance of truth-telling under broad general training rules to qualified suboptimality results focused on SW-Max rules. The conditional payment-equivalence claim is also extended beyond SW-Max to implementable rules satisfying continuity and an additional connecting condition.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly explains why affine payments do not cover nonadditive objectives such as Nash social welfare and MaxMin-RLHF. It adds that a fixed finite model set preserves DSIC but may violate the continuity condition, and drops v2's interpretation of nonoptimal training as optimal training for perturbed rewards.

D1.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 newly document LLaMA2-7B, supervised initialization, single-reward training followed by candidate-model combination, KL regularization, and reward rescaling. These provide an implementation outline beyond v2's conceptual approximations, but candidate counts, exact reward-model checkpoints, and detailed training settings remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning through facility-location connections, divergence theory, and additional multi-objective alignment and game research. It newly distinguishes Park et al.'s concurrent mechanism-design contribution, previously cited more generally, and adds works including Rewarded Soups, Multi-Objective Decoding, and MaxMin-RLHF.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around the economic scenario and SW-Max focus. Preliminaries and game formulation are separated, general-rule material moves to Appendix D, and the main theory, proofs, conclusion, and future-work discussion are reorganized beyond the insertion of new experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adds a motivating RLHF-game schematic (Figure 1) and an eight-panel logarithmic results plot with a shared legend (Figure 2). These are localized visual additions; the document otherwise retains its single-column text-and-equation layout, with no tables in either version.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's theoretical treatment, v3 adds a concrete implementation, empirical illustrations, and fuller normalization-dependent arguments. However, Theorem 4.3 omits restrictions required by its detailed counterpart, Theorem A.2, leaving a central revised claim inconsistently scoped. The experiments also omit important reproduction details. These practical and explanatory gains coexist with theoretical reliability concerns, preventing a confident net quality judgment.
